long_biography.plain_text:
Nyetimber became the platform for Eric Heerema’s long-term bet that English sparkling wine could compete at the highest level. After acquiring the historic Sussex estate in 2006, he recruited Canadian winemaking couple Cherie Spriggs and Brad Greatrix, enlarged its vineyard base and kept production reliant on company-owned grapes. Pressing, vinification and extended ageing were brought within the operation, giving the business tighter control over each vintage and supporting distinctive releases.

The capital behind that expansion came from inherited industrial wealth, not from wine. Heerema, a Dutch-trained lawyer and investor, was one of five brothers who succeeded to the offshore construction concern founded by Pieter Schelte Heerema; a sibling later bought the others’ interests. His teenage fascination with wine had already led him to plant vines on grazing land at his English property. In 2024, the Nyetimber group widened into spirits by purchasing The Lakes Distillery, adding English single-malt whisky while Heerema continued to direct the business and serve on its operating-company boards.
